solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's used to attach leaves and possibly petals close to flower

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of petals may be arranged some other way
the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A florist describes something that fixes leaves and petals near a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges PETALS into STAPLE; 'close to flower' adds its last letter, R. The leaves are sheets of paper, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stapler fixes sheets of paper together, and pages are often called leaves.

clue.text: One whose opinion is sought is talking wearily on the phone?

indicators.note: on the phone one is only heard, so the words count by their pronunciation

parts.note: to talk wearily is to sound bored: sounding bored

explanation.surface: Someone consulted for advice drones on tiredly during a call.
explanation.definitionFit: A sounding board is a person you try ideas out on to get a reaction.

clue.text: Being nimble is talent that's good for ballet, primarily

indicators.note: one letter stands for another, so it replaces it

parts.note: ability is talent

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter

explanation.surface: Being light on one's feet is a gift that suits a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's good for ballet, primarily' means G replaces B, the first letter of ballet, in ABILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Agility is nimbleness, the quality of being quick and light in movement.

clue.text: A no-hoper, one concludes first off

indicators.note: first off takes away the opening letter

parts.note: a closer is one who concludes

explanation.surface: A hopeless case sums up the matter right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' reads like 'to begin with', but it removes the first letter of CLOSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone with no chance of success, like a no-hoper.

clue.text: Esoteric artist's cultured but nameless

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: refined means cultured

explanation.surface: An obscure artist is sophisticated but anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefied means understood only by a select few, close to esoteric.

clue.text: Islander requires a short time in hospital

indicators.note: in places the short stay inside the word for hospital

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital
MO is a moment, as in 'wait a mo'

explanation.surface: Someone from an island needs a brief hospital stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Samoa in the Pacific is an islander.

clue.text: I had to come in to do vocals for short track

indicators.note: coming in means going inside, so these letters enter the singing

parts.note: to do vocals is to sing
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A session musician was called in to sing on a short recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'track' suggests a song, but it is a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A siding is a short stretch of railway track off the main line.

clue.text: Police tolerated a certain drug

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
had as in 'I won't have it', meaning put up with
one as in 'one Mr Smith', meaning a certain

explanation.surface: Officers turned a blind eye to a particular narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Methadone is a synthetic opioid, used to treat heroin addiction.

clue.text: SAS perhaps needs to reveal chain of command

parts.note: to air views is to reveal them
line as in line management, a chain of command

explanation.surface: The special forces must disclose who reports to whom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'SAS' suggests the British special forces, but it is Scandinavian Airlines.
explanation.definitionFit: SAS (Scandinavian Airlines) is an example of an air carrier.

clue.text: US enduring struggle to oust Government with no policies

indicators.note: a struggle throws things into disorder, so these letters are rearranged
ousting removes someone, so a letter is taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: America is fighting to throw out its government while having no policies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to oust Government' removes G from USENDURING; 'struggle' rearranges what remains. 'policies' are insurance policies, not political ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninsured holds no insurance policies.

clue.text: 'Brief Encounter' seriously enthrals

indicators.note: to enthral is literally to hold captive, so the phrase holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: The film Brief Encounter is said to grip its audience deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like part of the film title, but it is the definition; the letters run across encounTER SEriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse and brief both describe speech that uses few words.

clue.text: List of people getting local teller working with returning officer, for starters

indicators.note: working means in operation, worked into new form, so the letters are rearranged
starters are first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A register drawn up by a local vote counter with the returning officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning officer' reads as the election official, but only gives R and O to the anagram; nothing is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The electoral roll is the register of everyone entitled to vote.

clue.text: After Victor leaves, club is more dull

indicators.note: when Victor leaves, its letter departs from the word for club

parts.note: a driver is a golf club
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Once Victor departs, the club becomes a duller place.
explanation.definitionFit: Drier as a comparative means more dull or less lively, like a dry speech.

clue.text: Imagine the volume of some pop on the radio!

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the words are judged by how they are pronounced

parts.note: Fanta is a fizzy soft drink (pop), and its volume is its size: Fanta's size

explanation.surface: A listener marvels at how loud some pop music is on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' and 'pop' look like loudness and music, but they mean the size of a can of Fanta, a brand of fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To fantasize is to picture things in the mind, a synonym for imagine.

clue.text: Nationalist, say, bamboozled by philosopher? He refuses to agree

indicators.note: someone bamboozled is taken in, so this word goes inside the philosopher

parts.note: A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nationalist, for instance, is fooled by a thinker and won't go along with things.
explanation.definitionFit: A naysayer is a person who habitually objects or says no.

clue.text: Travelling around meant carrying correct change

indicators.note: carrying holds something within, so the rearranged letters go round the mending
travelling around moves the letters about

parts.note: to mend is to correct

explanation.surface: A traveller's money has to be swapped for correct change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' suggests coins, but means an alteration; 'Travelling around' rearranges the letters of 'meant' into AMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is an alteration, a change made to a text.

clue.text: Powerful businessman?

parts.note: read as a company gentleman: CO is company
GENT is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A mighty figure in the commercial world.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'businessman' is not a plain synonym but a playful split into a company and a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is forceful and convincing, so powerful in that sense.

clue.text: Sacked, having called in sick? On the contrary

indicators.note: in puts one word inside another
on the contrary swaps the order the clue states, so sick goes inside called

parts.note: paged means summoned, called
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Fired after phoning in ill?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' reads as dismissed from work, but it means plundered.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillaged means looted, the old sense of sacked, as in sacking a city.

clue.text: Missing Barnet, soundly wept

indicators.note: soundly means by sound, so the word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: Barnet is rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), and missing hair is bald

explanation.surface: Someone cried hard over a missing person or place called Barnet.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET is Cockney rhyming slang for hair, from Barnet Fair; Barnet is also a London borough and a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to cry loudly, so bawled means wept.

clue.text: Minority member of Scottish Church gets to use toilet without charge?

parts.note: to wee is to urinate
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A churchgoer from Scotland gets a public convenience at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wee Frees are the Free Church of Scotland, a small strict Presbyterian body that stayed out of the 1900 union.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wee Free is a nickname for a member of the minority Free Church of Scotland.

clue.text: One hushes up an incriminating report?

definitions.text: One hushes up an incriminating report?

parts.words: One hushes up an incriminating report?
parts.note: reads as someone covering up a damning document, but the report is a gunshot that a fitting on a gun muffles

explanation.walkthrough: 'report' suggests a document, but it is the bang of a gun, which a device on the barrel quietens.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's muffler deadens the noise of firing; also anyone who keeps others quiet.

clue.text: Emperor finally dons new clothes, mostly getting a laugh

indicators.note: donning means putting on, so the clothing goes round the last letter
new means made into a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged
mostly drops the final letter
finally takes the last letter

explanation.surface: The emperor finally puts on his new clothes, raising a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emperor finally' gives R; 'mostly' cuts CLOTHES to CLOTHE, which 'new' rearranges and 'dons' wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, a kind of laugh.

clue.text: Writer Hemingway perhaps promoting good man

indicators.note: promoting moves something up, so the saint is brought to the front

parts.note: Ernest is Hemingway's first name
ST is a saint, a good man

explanation.surface: An author, Hemingway for example, gets behind a decent fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century novelist who wrote Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Police act on lead based on hearsay

indicators.note: to police is to sort out or control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Officers follow up a tip-off that rests only on rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is a verb telling the solver to rearrange ACT ON LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence rests on stories people tell, rather than proof, so it comes from hearsay.

clue.text: Cook to get very excited about recipe

indicators.note: about puts the boiling around the letter for recipe

parts.note: to boil is to seethe with strong feeling
R is an abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe (take), as in Rx

explanation.surface: A chef grows agitated over a set of cooking instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Broiling is a way of cooking with direct heat, chiefly an American term for grilling.

clue.text: It's weaker than bloody Bass, mate!

parts.note: B abbreviates bass in music
an ally is a friend, a mate

explanation.surface: A drinker says a beer is weaker than a stout, mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody' is the British swear word; Bass is a British beer brand but here gives B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bally is a mild British euphemism standing in for the swear word bloody.

clue.text: A depressing number are into drug? That's about right

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the earlier pieces go round the letter for right

parts.note: to dig something is to like it, to be into it
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how many sad people are hooked on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a piece of music, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song, a gloomy piece of music.

clue.text: Old Balt sits in dress circle for opera

indicators.note: sitting in something means being inside it, so these letters go within the other pieces

parts.note: to rig out is to dress
O is a circle by its shape
a Lett is a Latvian, one of the Baltic peoples

explanation.surface: An elderly man from the Baltic takes a seat in the dress circle to watch an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress circle' looks like a theatre balcony, but splits into RIG and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's opera about a court jester.

clue.text: Red setter needs lead for example, having gone away previously

indicators.note: previously places the going-away piece before the rest

parts.note: left means departed, gone away
the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A red setter, a dog, needs a leash, as an illustration, having run off earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red setter' looks like the dog breed, but 'Red' is the definition and 'setter' the setter as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftie, a left-winger, is called a Red in political slang.

clue.text: Regularly visited dirty room of one inside for battery

indicators.note: only some letters at regular intervals are visited, the odd ones

parts.note: one inside is a prisoner, whose room is a cell

explanation.surface: Someone often went into a prisoner's filthy room to get a battery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry cell is a type of electric battery with a paste electrolyte rather than liquid.
